paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole sermon is about: Jesus cares about the inside. The scribes and Pharisees kept the outside SPARKLING. They had the tithes counted, the oath rules polished and the tombs decorated, but Jesus says the inside was "full of hypocrisy and wickedness" (Matthew 23:28). When the outside shines and the inside is a mess, that's a cookie box with a gorgeous bow on top and last month's crumbs underneath, and I've handed out a few of those myself.

Jesus doesn't tell them to drop the small things. He says they should have practiced "justice, mercy, and faithfulness," without neglecting the tithes (Matthew 23:23). So the lesson for you and me is to ask what's going on in the heart behind the rule. A rule that makes us look good while we ignore people in front of us has missed the point. I think that's why He says to "First clean the inside" (Matthew 23:26).

Now listen to how the sermon ends. After every woe, Jesus says, "how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!" (Matthew 23:37). I think that tells us the sharp words come from someone who wants people close, not someone who wants them gone. So when His Word shows you something inside that needs cleaning, friend, don't hide from it. Run to Him, because He is still the One who longs to gather His people in.
